# Labels (generated by scripts/run_preprocess.py — do not edit by hand)

STEW only provides **workload** information: the condition (rest `lo` / SIMKAP task `hi`) and a
self-reported workload rating (1–9) per recording. Subjects 5, 24 and 42 have no rating.
Masked labels are stored as `-1`; subjects are never dropped — each task uses its mask.

| Task | Column | Definition | Subjects |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 workload_binary | `y_binary` | lo = 0 (low), hi = 1 (high) | 48 |
| T2 workload_level | `y_level` | own rating 1–3 low, 4–6 medium, 7–9 high; unrated masked | 45 |
| T3 workload_within_task | `y_within` | hi recordings only: rating 4–6 moderate, 7–9 high; lo + unrated masked | 45 |

## Class counts

| Task | Unit | class counts | by condition (lo / hi) |
|---|---|---|---|
| T1 workload_binary | recordings | low 48, high 48 | lo: 48/0; hi: 0/48 |
| T2 workload_level | recordings | low 42, medium 23, high 25 | lo: 42/3/0; hi: 0/20/25 |
| T3 workload_within_task | recordings | moderate 20, high 25 | lo: 0/0; hi: 20/25 |
| T1 workload_binary | epochs | low 3552, high 3552 | lo: 3552/0; hi: 0/3552 |
| T2 workload_level | epochs | low 3108, medium 1702, high 1850 | lo: 3108/222/0; hi: 0/1480/1850 |
| T3 workload_within_task | epochs | moderate 1480, high 1850 | lo: 0/0; hi: 1480/1850 |

## Why T2 is confounded and T3 matters

For T2, rest recordings are low/medium/high = 42/3/0 and task recordings are 0/20/25. So a T2 classifier can score well just by detecting rest vs task (T1) — it says little about *graded* workload.

T3 uses only the task recordings, so both classes share the same condition, the same task and the same recording setup; only the self-reported workload differs. It is the confound-free workload task and is treated as a primary result, even though it has only 45 labelled recordings (one per rated subject), so its estimates are noisy. Because every subject contributes exactly one class in T3, per-subject metrics such as macro-F1 are undefined; T3 is evaluated on pooled out-of-fold predictions and on one aggregated prediction per subject.

Attention, fatigue and learning readiness have **no labels** in STEW. Their model heads exist but are masked off; the dashboard shows heuristic EEG indices for them instead.
